items.title: Chinese AI model Kimi K3.1 Pro is closing in on Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 55 points on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an 11-point jump over its predecessor that puts it in fourth place. Only three Anthropic and Meta models rank higher. If Moonshot releases the weights as planned, the gap between open and proprietary models shrinks to just three points....

items.title: Three-week on-site audit at OpenAI reveals major gaps in AI safety monitoring
items.summary: External auditors from METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks on-site at OpenAI examining the company's internal monitoring system for AI agents and found significant gaps, with up to 25 percent of agent traffic from models at the GPT-5.5 class and above going unmonitored. OpenAI redacted large portions of the 61-page report, and only a summary is publicly available....

items.title: Anthropic says its unreleased model is both more capable and better aligned than Mythos 5.1
items.summary: Anthropic says it has an internal AI model that outperforms and is better aligned than Mythos 5.1. During a cybersecurity test by the UK's AISI, Mythos 5 went rogue in 9 of 43 runs, sneaking malicious code into a real GitHub project and creating fake accounts to get it approved. An internal research model stopped such attacks on its own 67 percent of the time....

items.title: Anthropic Adds Opt-In Security Scanning for Critical Open-Source Projects
items.summary: AI company Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service to find vulnerabilities in open-source projects. Enrolled maintainers receive periodic security reports generated by the company's strongest models, including Claude Mythos. The reports are sent without human review, and project maintainers can choose to validate their findings and decide which proposed fixes to accept. By Matt Saunders

items.title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
items.summary: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?

items.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
items.summary: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.

items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says advanced AI will inevitably escape its sandbox, and only alignment can save us
items.summary: Sam Altman believes advanced AI can't be kept locked up forever. Sandboxes and monitoring are only temporary fixes. Eventually, the only real solution is alignment, and that's still an unsolved problem. He also warns that AI models are already finding hardware security flaws no human hacker would ever spot....

items.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner to advance AI safety and security
items.summary: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK are partnering on AI safety, security, and technical research to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem.

items.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
items.summary: OpenAI explains how we strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation, including offline environments and high-compute red-teaming.

items.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
items.summary: OpenAI and Google Cloud are bringing frontier models and Codex workflows to Gemini’s Model Garden, available through Google Cloud Marketplace.

items.title: Democratic governance of frontier AI, part II: Empowering cyber defenders
items.summary: OpenAI outlines a blueprint for empowering cyber defenders with frontier AI, stronger safeguards, modernized cybersecurity, and more resilient public institutions.

items.title: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’
items.summary: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
